clue.text: Fruit and nuts returned by boy

indicators.note: returned means the word for nuts is sent back the way it came, read right to left

parts.note: nuts means crazy, mad
a boy is a son

explanation.surface: A snack of fruit and nuts handed back by a lad.
explanation.definitionFit: A small dark purple plum, so a kind of fruit.

clue.text: Going round fields is utter delight

indicators.note: going round means the word for utter encircles the word for fields

parts.note: utter in the sense of complete or sheer means pure
leas are meadows or fields, a poetic word

explanation.surface: Wandering about in the fields is a total joy.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: both mean enjoyment or gratification.

clue.text: Stuck in boggy area, everyone stumbled

indicators.note: stuck in means the word for everyone is placed inside the word for a boggy area

parts.note: a fen is low marshy land
everyone means all

explanation.surface: Everybody got stuck in a bog and tripped over.
explanation.definitionFit: Having stumbled and gone down is to have tumbled to the ground; both are past forms of a verb of toppling.

clue.text: Container of cash found in lowly French prison once

indicators.note: found in means the cash container sits inside the word for lowly

parts.note: lowly means base, of humble rank
a till is a cash drawer in a shop

explanation.surface: A cash box turns up in a humble jail in old France.
explanation.definitionFit: The Paris fortress-jail stormed in 1789 at the start of the Revolution.

clue.text: I study computer symbol

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart, an old verb

explanation.surface: A student says they are examining a symbol on the computer.
explanation.definitionFit: A small picture on a screen standing for a program or file.

clue.text: Mending one article mislaid by giant chap in disarray

indicators.note: mislaid by says the article is lost from the letters that follow
in disarray means the remaining letters are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A huge man in a muddle has lost something while doing repairs.
explanation.walkthrough: Take one A from GIANTCHAP ('mislaid by') and shuffle what is left ('in disarray') to get the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Repairing a hole by sewing on a piece of material is a way of mending.

clue.text: Official document reveals the old man's game

parts.note: the old man is a familiar term for father, pa, so the old man's gives pa's
a game is a sport

explanation.surface: Paperwork exposes what Dad likes to play.
explanation.definitionFit: The government-issued travel paper is an official document.

clue.text: Vessel full of animals seen near southern island

parts.note: Noah's ark carried the animals two by two

explanation.surface: A boat crammed with creatures is sighted by an island in the south.
explanation.walkthrough: SARK is one of the Channel Islands, between England and France.
explanation.definitionFit: A small Channel Island is an example of an island.

clue.text: Did lively dance round about, becoming tired

indicators.note: round means the dance word goes around the word for about

parts.note: to jig is to do a lively dance, so did one is jigged
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Someone danced a jig around and wore themselves out.
explanation.walkthrough: JIGGERED is British slang for exhausted.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British synonym for worn out or exhausted.

clue.text: Give teacher top grade before half term

indicators.note: before means the earlier pieces come ahead of the last one

parts.note: a don is a university teacher
A is the top grade in exams

indicators.note: half means only the first two of the four letters of term are used

explanation.surface: Hand the teacher an A grade before the term is half over.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to give money or goods to a cause.

clue.text: Councillor meets top journalist — he's owed money

parts.note: the editor is the senior journalist on a paper

explanation.surface: A local councillor meets the newspaper's editor, who is owed cash.
explanation.definitionFit: A lender or anyone to whom a debt is due.

clue.text: Witness at international cricket match

parts.note: a Test is a full international cricket match

explanation.surface: A spectator at a Test match.
explanation.definitionFit: As verbs, to witness a document and to certify it are synonyms.

clue.text: Getting up, mischievous type put on a jumper

indicators.note: put on means the a is placed after, below, in this down clue
getting up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: an elf is a mischievous sprite

explanation.surface: Rising, a prankster pulls on a sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumper' looks like a British sweater, but it means something that jumps.
explanation.definitionFit: A small insect famous for its leaping, so a jumper.

clue.text: Experiences sounds of bells in battle site

parts.note: to experience something is to have it, so experiences gives has
tings are light ringing sounds as from bells

explanation.surface: Someone hears bells ringing on an old battlefield.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1066 battle took place near this Sussex town, so it names a battlefield.

clue.text: Exercise on bar, one way or the other

definitions.note: the gym move of hauling yourself up to a horizontal bar, which here also serves as the whole wordplay

indicators.note: one way or the other says the word reads the same forwards and backwards

parts.note: the gym move of hauling yourself up to a horizontal bar, which here also serves as the whole wordplay

explanation.surface: A gym move on a bar, done either way.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising oneself by the arms to a horizontal bar is a gym exercise.

clue.text: Abandon one's country, there's something wrong

definitions.meaning: to desert one's nation for another, verb sense
a flaw or fault, noun sense

explanation.surface: Leaving your homeland means something has gone wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to desert one's state; the noun means a flaw.

clue.text: Head away from modest shopping arcade

indicators.note: head away from means the first letter of the word for modest is dropped

parts.note: modest in size means small

explanation.surface: A boss leaves a humble little shopping precinct.
explanation.definitionFit: A covered shopping centre or precinct, like an arcade.

clue.text: What very modest cruise company has? That's a joke

definitions.text: What very modest cruise company has
definitions.meaning: a tiny cruise firm would own just a single ship
a short quip delivered in a single sentence

explanation.surface: A wisecrack about a cruise firm too small to have a fleet.
explanation.definitionFit: A quip told in a sentence; read literally, a single ocean ship.

clue.text: Cry briefly, then cry again after a sleep

indicators.note: after means the second cry word follows the a
briefly means the word cry is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a second word for cry here is shout

explanation.surface: Someone sobs for a moment, then yells again after a nap.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal phrasal verb meaning to fall asleep quickly from exhaustion.

clue.text: Introductions for an indie rock song

indicators.note: introductions means the opening letter of each of the next three words

explanation.surface: Opening bars of an indie rock track.
explanation.definitionFit: A tune or melody, as in a simple song.

clue.text: Overexcitement spreading this year

indicators.note: spreading means the letters of the two words are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Wild fervour is catching on this year.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncontrolled emotional frenzy, a state of extreme excitement.

clue.text: Thing to mind

definitions.meaning: an article or item, noun sense
to mind in the sense of disapproving or protesting, verb sense

explanation.definitionFit: The noun means an item; the verb means to raise an objection.

clue.text: Fancy gadget with label attached

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate or remade, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A posh gizmo comes with a price tag.
explanation.definitionFit: Labelled: fitted with a tag or ticket.

clue.text: Sickly-looking friend has little energy

parts.note: a pal is a friend
E is the physics symbol for energy, a little bit of it

explanation.surface: A wan-looking mate is low on energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Pallid in complexion, as someone unwell looks.

clue.text: Regularly went round school

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of the two words is taken

explanation.surface: Someone did the rounds of the school routinely.
explanation.walkthrough: ETON is the famous English boarding school near Windsor.
explanation.definitionFit: The well-known English public school, so an example of a school.
